CHIEF COMPLAINT
Upper respiratory infection

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
59-year-old male presents with upper respiratory infection symptoms that began after yard work approximately one week ago. Patient reports initial fatigue and shortness of breath with exertion, specifically while lifting heavy bags of soil during landscaping activities. Denies productive cough at this time but anticipates cough may develop. Reports feeling warm but attributed this to exertion. Denies fever. Also reports elbow pain and knee soreness, which patient attributes to physical labor from lifting bags. Patient has received both COVID vaccines.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies seasonal allergies. Denies nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Reports muscle aches and joint pain as described above. No other symptoms reported.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Depression
Type 2 diabetes mellitus
Hypertension

MEDICATIONS
Metformin (to be increased to 1000 mg twice daily)
Lisinopril 20 mg daily

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient performs yard work and landscaping. Wife enrolled patient in barre classes to help with relaxation. Monitoring of blood pressure and blood glucose occurs regularly during work week but less consistently on weekends. Diet generally good with occasional lapses during social events.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs normal, no fever. Heart sounds normal and strong. Lungs with scattered rhonchi bilaterally that clear with cough. Lower extremity edema noted. Elbow pain on palpation bilaterally.

RESULTS
Chest X-ray: No airspace disease, no pneumonia.
Hemoglobin A1C: 8.0 (elevated)

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Upper respiratory infection/viral syndrome: Patient does not have pneumonia on chest imaging. Will send COVID test to rule out COVID-19. Advised symptoms should resolve in a couple days. Prescribed Robitussin for cough. Advised to take ibuprofen and acetaminophen as needed for fever.
2. Depression: Currently managing well with barre classes. Offered medication management or psychotherapy referral. Patient declined for now, will reassess in a few months.
3. Type 2 diabetes mellitus: Hemoglobin A1C elevated at 8.0; goal is 6-7. Increasing metformin to 1000 mg twice daily. Will recheck hemoglobin A1C in four months.
4. Hypertension: Currently well controlled on current regimen. Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily. Refill ordered. Lipid panel ordered.
Follow-up appointment in four months.
